providers.sourceStatusReason: Unofficial WATCH source: every scheduled, startup, restart, ordinary manual, and dedicated-repair Claude collection first rereads exact native credentials noninteractively, preferring a usable file session. If recovery is required, that collection has one bounded opportunity for screen-unlocked native authorization and, for expired or rejected credentials, one Claude Code owner /usage launch. Denial aborts the current attempt without a loop; the next default five-minute cycle may retry. Only claudeAiOauth is eligible, MCP is forbidden, and only a successful live response is fresh.
documentation: https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64/2.1.280 (reset query and cedar_ember grant schema; published SHA-512 integrity verified)
providers.credentialPersistence: Claude-owned ~/.claude/.credentials.json and native Keychain generic-password service Claude Code-credentials with account NSUserName(); Token Jar performs exact read-only access and keeps no Claude credential or usage cache, while Claude Code alone may rotate its stores under .oauth_refresh.lock during a bounded collection recovery
tokenTankIO: Read claudeAiOauth only from ~/.claude/.credentials.json and the native generic-password service Claude Code-credentials with account NSUserName(); never match another same-service account. Require user:profile, finite positive expiry more than 60 seconds away, and reject MCP

Every Claude collection first rereads the exact file noninteractively, then the exact Keychain account when no usable file session exists. Retain rejected-token identity independently per file/Keychain slot and adopt a changed valid external token. On expiry at 60 seconds or less or usage HTTP 401, retry usage at most once only with a changed token; HTTP 403 never recovers

Scheduled refresh, ordinary user refresh, startup, restart, and dedicated repair all use collection context allowsClaudeRecovery=true. isUserInitiated truthfully records the trigger and does not control recovery authority; the default schedule remains five minutes

When a bounded recovery cannot supply a usable session, retain the prior in-memory snapshot only as stale and expose typed repairClaudeConnection for unavailable Keychain access or a session still needing recovery. Missing or revoked login requires source-owner sign-in

Each collection has at most one recovery opportunity. After the screen-unlocked guard, it may attempt native authorization once and, for expired or rejected credentials, launch one bounded owner process. Denial, cancellation, lock, or authorization failure aborts the current attempt without another CLI or prompt loop; the next scheduled collection may try again

The localized Repair Claude Connection / Claude 연결 복구 action starts an immediate manual collection under the same limits. Concurrent repair callers coalesce. The UI immediately shows pending manual repair or active collection progress with native approval guidance, without inferring internal phases

Claude Code may show its own permission UI during the single bounded owner launch. The owner uses fixed absolute executable candidates, an empty mode-0700 workspace, minimal fixed environment, fixed safe-mode/no-tools arguments, fixed bounded timeout, and the official owner refresh lock

Prompt veto precedes readiness and success. Require readiness plus shift+tab before exactly /usage and a completed panel plus one second quiet; trust is accepted only in the verified-empty workspace and never after /usage. Completed flow sends Esc then /exit with five-second grace; the post-usage hard deadline is passive and pre-readiness cleanup supplies no input

GET only https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, optionally same-token /api/oauth/profile, and optionally same-token /api/oauth/usage?cedar_ember=1&skip_spend=1 with a 15-second maximum. The reset request uses only the exact fixed query, no body, no authentication recovery, and no redemption POST. Parse cedar_ember.grants id/resets_left/starts_at/ends_at; preserve explicit counts without local-date ownership filtering. Empty grants without eligible:true, absent or malformed metadata stay unknown without discarding valid usage. Do not import browser cookies, automate login/browser approval, scrape PTY usage, call Admin or inference APIs, use ~/.claude.json cached usage, or directly POST/write/copy/cache a Claude token
externalPaths: native Keychain generic-password service Claude Code-credentials; account NSUserName() only
providers.tccClass: none; native Keychain authorization is available at most once per collection recovery after the screen-unlocked guard. providers.selectedSource: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json OIDC session; when access expiry is within 60 seconds or the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, refresh_token grant at fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token and atomic same-file rotation, then one proxy retry; primary cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits; only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, bearer-only POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same session bearer and a 6-second timeout
providers.sourceStatusReason: The Grok CLI owner session and CLI-proxy credits endpoint remain primary. Unlike CodexBar, which is only a reference for credits behavior and does not directly refresh OAuth, Token Jar performs the user-approved narrow renewal: an OIDC access token expiring within 60 seconds, or one rejected by the first proxy request with 401/403, is renewed once through the official fixed token endpoint after exact issuer and selected client/scope checks; the rotated session is atomically preserved to the same owner file before one proxy retry. Only a successful proxy snapshot with unknown usage may trigger the existing same-session bearer-only gRPC-web billing fallback. Proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity remain authoritative; web billing supplies usage only. Token Jar never imports browser cookies, uses Grok ACP stdio or a CLI subprocess, offers manual-token UI, calls the xAI Management prepaid-balance API, or caches tokens in Keychain.
providers.rejectedAlternative: Browser-cookie imports, Grok ACP stdio, CLI subprocess or interactive automation, manual-token UI, local-session estimates, xAI Management API/prepaid-balance calls, Keychain token caches, backups, other secret stores, and arbitrary credential copying remain prohibited. The older Grok Build ACP x.ai/billing probe returned JSON-RPC -32601 (method-not-found) on official Grok 1.0.13.
providers.credentialOwner: Grok CLI, with user-approved Token Jar renewal of the selected OIDC entry
providers.credentialPersistence: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json; Token Jar may atomically replace only that same file after a successful official refresh_token grant, preserving the optional rotated refresh token and updated expires_at; no backup, copy, or other secret store
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.grok/auth.json through the Grok-scoped session capability; require issuer https://auth.x.ai and exact agreement between the selected client/scope suffix and the entry's non-empty oidc_client_id

When expires_at is within 60 seconds, or only after the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, POST a refresh_token grant to fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token with public-client authentication, no cookies, and no redirects

Once renewal starts, hold a bounded token-free lock shared only by Token Jar processes across reread, rotation, comparison, and persistence. Install the cancellation handler before checking cancellation so cancellation before waiter registration still seals the waiter gate. A started transaction settles before a canceled observer receives CancellationError; pre-start cancellation aborts
HTTPS GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with the selected ephemeral bearer; after 401/403 renewal, retry this proxy exactly once

Only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same selected bearer, a 5-byte empty gRPC-web data frame (00 00 00 00 00), no cookies, and a 6-second timeout

Preserve proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity; adopt a published web percentage, or an omitted proto3 scalar as zero only for a structurally complete response with a recognized current weekly/monthly period containing the refresh time; otherwise retain unknown, including a failed fallback
Expose published creditUsagePercent or the same-row on-demand used/cap ratio under the credits quota
Display only the selected auth entry's optional email in memory; never infer identity from another entry or token
providers.liveValidation: Historical Grok renewal/usage evidence remains scoped to its original revision. After the cancellation repair, package 172/12 passed three consecutive runs and app 35/full UI 19 reran and passed. Repair-commit CI remains pending.
providers.mutationRisk: The only credential mutation allowed is successful Grok renewal written atomically to the same ~/.grok/auth.json through a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file. A bounded token-free lock covers reread, HTTP rotation, comparison, and persistence among Token Jar processes; once renewal starts it settles despite observer cancellation, after which a canceled observer receives CancellationError after commit, while pre-start cancellation aborts. Comparison detects observable external rotation and prefers a newer session but cannot close the final rename window against an uncooperative concurrent Grok CLI writer; the lock is not claimed to be CLI-honored. No backup, other secret store, cookie import, Management API fallback, or unrelated source-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: WATCH: live-validate a naturally near-expiry event, real proxy HTTP 401/403 renewal, concurrent real Grok CLI rotation, missing/revoked versus network-error recovery, and the packaged final candidate on supported OS versions; complete CI, signing, and notarization evidence
